nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finitely supported real sequence indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, let $q$ be a positive integer, and let $a$ be a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$, represented by its least nonnegative residue. Then the absolute value of the discrepancy of $\alpha$ at modulus $q$ and residue $a$ is at most the primitive discrepancy of $\alpha$ at modulus $q$.
nodes.title: Primitive residue-class discrepancies are bounded by the primitive discrepancy

nodes.summary: For every finitely supported real sequence $\alpha$ indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, the averaged discrepancy of $\alpha$ with cutoff $Q = 0$ equals $0$, since there are no positive moduli $q \le 0$.
nodes.title: The averaged discrepancy with cutoff zero vanishes

nodes.summary: For a finitely supported real sequence $\alpha$ indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ and a natural number $Q$, the averaged discrepancy of $\alpha$ up to $Q$ is the sum $\sum_{q=1}^{Q} \Delta^*(\alpha; q)$, where $\Delta^*(\alpha; q)$ is the primitive discrepancy of $\alpha$ at modulus $q$.
nodes.title: Averaged discrepancy

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $\alpha, \beta \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be finitely supported. Then their convolution $\alpha \star \beta$ has value $0$ at index $0$.
nodes.title: The multiplicative convolution vanishes at index zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $\alpha, \beta \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be finitely supported, with convolution $\alpha \star \beta$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
nodes.title: Coefficients of the multiplicative convolution

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring, let $v \in R$, and let $\beta \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be finitely supported. If $e$ is the sequence with value $v$ at index $0$ and $0$ at every other index, then the convolution $e \star \beta$ is the zero sequence.
nodes.title: Convolving a sequence supported at zero gives zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring, let $\alpha \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be finitely supported, and let $v \in R$. If $e$ is the sequence with value $v$ at index $0$ and $0$ at every other index, then the convolution $\alpha \star e$ is the zero sequence.
nodes.title: Convolving with a sequence supported at zero gives zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $\alpha, \beta \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be finitely supported. Their convolution $\alpha \star \beta$ is the finitely supported sequence whose value at $n$ is $\sum_{a, b \ge 1,\ ab = n} \alpha(a)\beta(b)$; the values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ at index $0$ are discarded.
nodes.title: Multiplicative convolution of finitely supported sequences

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $v \in K$, let $q$ be a positive integer and let $a \in \mathbb{N}$. The sequence with value $v$ at index $0$ and $0$ at every other index has discrepancy $0$ at modulus $q$ and residue $a$.
nodes.title: A sequence supported at index zero has zero discrepancy

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $n$ be a positive integer, let $v \in K$, let $q$ be a positive integer and let $a \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $e$ be the sequence with value $v$ at index $n$ and $0$ at every other index. Then the discrepancy of $e$ at modulus $q$ and residue $a$ equals $A - B/\varphi(q)$, where $A = v$ if $n \equiv a \pmod{q}$ and $A = 0$ otherwise, $B = v$ if $\gcd(n, q) = 1$ and $B = 0$…
nodes.title: Discrepancy of a single positive term

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to K$ be finitely supported, let $q$ be a positive integer and let $a$ be a natural number. The discrepancy of $\alpha$ in the residue class of $a$ modulo $q$ is
nodes.title: Discrepancy in a residue class

nodes.summary: For every real $x > 0$ and every natural number $n$, the von Mangoldt function on the dyadic interval for $x$ takes at $n$ the value $\Lambda(n)$ if $x \le n \le 2x$, and $0$ otherwise, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function.
nodes.title: Values of the dyadic von Mangoldt function

nodes.summary: For a real number $x$, this is the finitely supported function on $\mathbb{N}$ whose value at $n$ is $\Lambda(n)$ when $n \ge 1$ and $x \le n \le 2x$, and $0$ otherwise, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function.
nodes.title: Von Mangoldt function on a dyadic interval

nodes.summary: For every finitely supported sequence $\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every positive integer $q$, there is a residue class $a$ modulo $q$ coprime to $q$ such that the primitive discrepancy of $\alpha$ modulo $q$ equals $|\Delta(\alpha; a \bmod q)|$, the absolute value of the discrepancy of $\alpha$ in the residue class of $a$ modulo $q$.
nodes.title: The primitive discrepancy is attained

nodes.summary: For a finitely supported sequence $\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer $q$, the primitive discrepancy of $\alpha$ modulo $q$ is the maximum, over the residue classes $a$ modulo $q$ that are coprime to $q$, of $|\Delta(\alpha; a \bmod q)|$, where $\Delta(\alpha; a \bmod q)$ is the discrepancy of $\alpha$ in the residue class of $a$ modulo $q$.
nodes.title: Primitive discrepancy
